tools.title: Tools
tools.backupDescription: Generates a gzipped SQL dump of the whole database — people, sources, citations, and the family tree graph — in one file. Restore it from the "Restore database" tool in the sidebar (a plain psql < file won't work — the family tree graph needs a couple of extra steps the restore tool already handles). You'll get a notification (top right) once it's ready to download.
tools.queuedLargeTree: Queued — this can take a little while for a large tree.
tools.albumZipDescription: Zips every photo in every album for a separate backup of your photo library. You'll get one notification per file if it needs more than one archive.
tools.queuedLargeLibrary: Queued — this can take a little while for a large library.
tools.restoreWarning: This overwrites your entire database with the contents of the file you upload. Other people using the app at the same time may see errors while this runs. Everyone, including you, will be signed out afterward — the restored data includes old sign-in sessions, not whoever's currently logged in. This cannot be undone.
tools.restoreUploadHint: Upload a .sql.gz file previously downloaded from the backup tool above.
tools.dropBackupFile: Drag a backup file here, or
tools.restoreQueued: Queued — you'll get a notification once it's done (or failed).
tools.faceRescanDescription: Asks Immich to re-run face detection across your whole photo library. Immich already does this automatically for new uploads — use this if a photo was added before face recognition was enabled, or a face didn't get picked up the first time. Detection itself runs in Immich's own background jobs, so this can take a while for a large library; you'll get a notification (top right) once every photo has been resubmitted.
tools.gedcomDescription: Exports every person, name, event, family, source, and citation as a standard GEDCOM 5.5.1 file — importable into most other genealogy software. Photos aren't included: they live in Immich, which GEDCOM has no way to reference.
tools.gedcomVersion551Hint: Read by almost every genealogy program — the safe choice.
tools.gedcomVersion70Hint: The newest standard. Check that the program you're sending it to can read GEDCOM 7.

gedcomImport.description: Adds the people, names, events, families, sources and citations from a GEDCOM file (exported from FamilySearch, Ancestry, MyHeritage, Gramps, or this app) to your tree. Pick a file to see what it contains first — nothing is saved until you press Import.
gedcomImport.backupHint: Everyone in the file is added as a new person, even if they're already in your tree — likely duplicates are listed below so you can decide before importing. An import can only be undone by restoring a backup, so consider taking one first.
gedcomImport.tooLarge: This file is too large to import in one go.

warning.malformedLine_one: {{count}} line couldn't be read and will be skipped
warning.malformedLine_other: {{count}} lines couldn't be read and will be skipped
warning.legacyEncoding_one: The file isn't UTF-8 — it was read as Windows "ANSI" text. Check that letters like æ, ø and å look right after importing.
warning.legacyEncoding_other: The file isn't UTF-8 — it was read as Windows "ANSI" text. Check that letters like æ, ø and å look right after importing.
warning.unparsedDate_one: {{count}} date couldn't be interpreted — its wording is kept, but it won't sort or count towards ages
warning.unparsedDate_other: {{count}} dates couldn't be interpreted — their wording is kept, but they won't sort or count towards ages
warning.missingReference_one: {{count}} reference points to a record that isn't in the file and will be skipped
warning.missingReference_other: {{count}} references point to records that aren't in the file and will be skipped
warning.extraVitalEvent_one: {{count}} person has more than one birth or death — the extra one is kept as an "other" event
warning.extraVitalEvent_other: {{count}} people have more than one birth or death — the extra ones are kept as "other" events
warning.inlineSource_one: {{count}} citation describes its source inline — it becomes a source of its own
warning.inlineSource_other: {{count}} citations describe their source inline — each becomes a source of its own
warning.sourceTextDropped_one: {{count}} source has notes or transcribed text, which aren't imported
warning.sourceTextDropped_other: {{count}} sources have notes or transcribed text, which aren't imported
warning.familyDataDropped_one: {{count}} family has marriage details or citations but not two partners, so they aren't imported
warning.familyDataDropped_other: {{count}} families have marriage details or citations but not two partners, so they aren't imported
warning.inferredDeceased_one: {{count}} person with no recorded death was born over 110 years ago and will be marked as deceased
warning.inferredDeceased_other: {{count}} people with no recorded death were born over 110 years ago and will be marked as deceased
warning.skippedTag_one: {{count}} entry of a kind this app doesn't store yet (photos, FamilySearch IDs, repository details, custom tags, …) will be skipped
warning.skippedTag_other: {{count}} entries of kinds this app doesn't store yet (photos, FamilySearch IDs, repository details, custom tags, …) will be skipped
warning.extraFamilyEvent_one: {{count}} family event beyond a marriage's start and end (an engagement, banns, a second marriage record) is kept as a line in that marriage's notes
warning.extraFamilyEvent_other: {{count}} family events beyond a marriage's start and end (engagements, banns, second marriage records) are kept as lines in those marriages' notes
warning.challengedParentLink_one: {{count}} parent link is marked as challenged in the file — it's imported, but worth checking
warning.challengedParentLink_other: {{count}} parent links are marked as challenged in the file — they're imported, but worth checking
warning.disprovenParentLink_one: {{count}} parent link is marked as disproven in the file and won't be imported
warning.disprovenParentLink_other: {{count}} parent links are marked as disproven in the file and won't be imported
warning.invalidCoordinates_one: {{count}} place has coordinates that couldn't be read, so they're skipped (the place name is kept)
warning.invalidCoordinates_other: {{count}} places have coordinates that couldn't be read, so they're skipped (the place names are kept)
warning.conflictingCoordinates_one: {{count}} place appears with different coordinates in different records — the first is used
warning.conflictingCoordinates_other: {{count}} places appear with different coordinates in different records — the first is used

tools.dataIntegrityDescription: A read-only report: citations pointing at a deleted name/event/union, people who might be duplicates, and (if Immich is configured) links pointing at a deleted Immich person. Nothing here is changed automatically — each finding is for you to judge.
tools.danglingCitationText: A citation from "{{source}}" references a deleted {{factType}} —
tools.danglingImmichLinkText: is linked to an Immich person that no longer exists.
tools.graphConsistencyDescription: Compares every person in the database against the family-tree graph that stores how they're related. A mismatch here means the two have drifted apart — read-only, nothing is changed automatically.
tools.orphanedGraphNodes: Graph nodes with no matching person
